question: Can the J7G additive red-X model hold initial error, complete first record, future physical-fault key and final physical support all fixed while changing only the public correction action?
role: Bounded identifiability prerequisite, not a new Born-law or schedule experiment
source_basis: Jing Appendix A.2/A.4 red-X and correction support convention
J7G exact finite history contrast with branch-specific future faults

model.support_law: Within the same fixed physical red-edge basis, final support S = E xor A xor F, with E the private initial red-X set, A the applied public red-X correction set and F the later private physical red-X fault set
model.first_boundary: The J7G complete first public record is fixed before action; no first-measurement resampling, posterior conditioning or hidden relation oracle is introduced
model.physical_and_public: A is public and relation-free; E and F are private exogenous keys; the audit may inspect them only as private model diagnostics. A different final support may have a different next public flux record, and the audit is not itself a complete Born law
model.proof_target: For common E and F, S(A1)=S(A2) implies A1=A2 by xor cancellation. Thus a distinct-action same-future-key comparison cannot also match final physical support in this additive model. A same-final-support distinct-action comparison requires F1 xor F2 = A1 xor A2
model.independent_unit_uncertainty: Finite deterministic algebraic audit; no stochastic sampling unit or uncertainty interval

matrix.primary_cells: All four action by future-key cells with exact final support and public flux from the pinned periodic red-edge map
matrix.exhaustive_control: All 8 correction subsets of [0,4,3] crossed with no future fault or one of the same three red edges: 32 cells, 112 distinct-action same-future comparisons; every such pair must have distinct final support
matrix.j7g_reproduction: The [0]/[0] and [4]/[4] diagonal cells exactly reproduce J7G's matched final support [0,4,3]; their different future keys prevent action-only causal attribution
matrix.classify_forks: Same-future-key distinct-action total effect may be defined only without matched final support; same-final-support history sensitivity may be defined only with branch-specific future faults. They are different estimands, not two rankings for a human to choose before the algebra is checked

competing_outcomes.identifiability_boundary_confirmed: All pins and 32-cell controls pass; record the impossibility of matching both F and final support for distinct A and route any subsequent causal action study to a separately registered same-future-key estimand without conditioning on final support
competing_outcomes.model_or_implementation_conflict: Any xor cancellation, source mapping, J7G reproduction or pin fails; censor causal interpretation and do not silently revise J7G's finite ideal result
competing_outcomes.unresolved: If public record equivalence differs from physical-support equivalence, retain this support-level proof only; no public-law or causal decoder benefit follows

acceptance: Five source/caller/result pins pass before and after
All four primary cells reproduce their algebraic support and eligible public flux; J7G diagonal support recovers exactly
All 32 control cells and 112 distinct-action same-future comparisons satisfy cancellation and distinct-final-support gates
The record separates a same-future-key action estimand from a same-final-support history estimand and does not promote either to a performance claim
No Born-law sampling, stochastic history, arm evaluation, bootstrap or caller mutation
stop_rule: Stop on any pin, support/flux, J7G reproduction, enumeration or 10-CPU-second cap failure. Do not fit a law, sample histories, extend geometry, invoke the frozen caller or claim action causality from J7G.
